Count days above (or below) a threshold in each season-year

Source: R/count-exceedances.R
count_exceedances.Rd

The general engine behind count_hot_days(). Works on any data frame of daily values, from any source, with any column names: count very hot days, mild days, heavy-rain days or cold nights, in a calendar year, a July-June year or a custom season. Missing days are counted against each season's coverage, so seasons with gaps are flagged rather than silently undercounted.

Usage

count_exceedances(
  data,
  value,
  threshold,
  direction = c("above", "below"),
  date = "date",
  start_month = 1,
  months = 1:12,
  min_coverage = 0.9
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per day for a single place. Filter to one place before calling (see the examples).

value

The name of the column holding the daily value, in quotes, for example "max_temp".

threshold

The value to compare each day against.

direction

"above" counts days at or above threshold; "below" counts days at or below it.

date

The name of the column holding dates (class Date), in quotes. Defaults to "date".

start_month

The month each season-year starts (1 to 12). Defaults to 1, an ordinary calendar year. Use 9 for the southern fire season, 7 for a July-June year.

months

The months to include. Defaults to all 12. For example, c(12, 1, 2) keeps only summer.

min_coverage

The share of days in a season that must have a value for the season to be marked complete. Defaults to 0.9.

Value

A tibble with one row per season-year and columns season_start, season (a label such as "2018-19", or "2018" for calendar years), days_possible, days_recorded, coverage, n_exceed (days meeting the threshold), extreme (the highest value for "above", the lowest for "below") and complete.

Examples

# Your own data can have any column names
sydney <- fire_season_temps |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Sydney") |>
  dplyr::select(day = date, tmax = max_temp)

# Summer days of 35 degrees C or more, Dec-Feb seasons
count_exceedances(sydney, "tmax", threshold = 35, date = "day",
                  start_month = 12, months = c(12, 1, 2)) |>
  tail()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   season_start season  days_possible days_recorded coverage n_exceed extreme
#>          <int> <chr>           <int>         <int>    <dbl>    <int>   <dbl>
#> 1         2013 2013-14            90            90        1        2    36.5
#> 2         2014 2014-15            90            90        1        1    35.7
#> 3         2015 2015-16            91            91        1        3    39.2
#> 4         2016 2016-17            90            90        1       11    39.4
#> 5         2017 2017-18            90            90        1        5    43.4
#> 6         2018 2018-19            90            90        1        4    39.6
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: complete <lgl>

# Mild summer days (maximum of 22 degrees C or less) are the opposite end
count_exceedances(sydney, "tmax", threshold = 22, direction = "below",
                  date = "day", start_month = 12, months = c(12, 1, 2)) |>
  tail()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   season_start season  days_possible days_recorded coverage n_exceed extreme
#>          <int> <chr>           <int>         <int>    <dbl>    <int>   <dbl>
#> 1         2013 2013-14            90            90        1        4    21.5
#> 2         2014 2014-15            90            90        1        5    20.4
#> 3         2015 2015-16            91            91        1        5    18.6
#> 4         2016 2016-17            90            90        1        3    19.1
#> 5         2017 2017-18            90            90        1        3    18.6
#> 6         2018 2018-19            90            90        1        2    21.1
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: complete <lgl>
